task_instance: Given a simulated user request describing a SaaS customer-support system that needs to handle billing, technical, and sales tickets, apply the multi-agent-patterns skill to produce a concrete multi-agent architecture design: decide whether multiple agents are justified, choose a pattern (supervisor/swarm/hierarchical), specify the context isolation mechanism, the handoff/telephone-game mitigation, error-propagation/validation controls, TTL limits, and consensus needs, citing which part of the skill drove each decision.
evidence: Created /tmp/claude-0/.../exec_div/muratcankoylan__agent-skills-for-context-engineering__multi-agent-patterns@office-assistant/request.md (the sample user request) and design.md (the deliverable). design.md walks through every decision point the skill requires: justification check against 'When to Activate' triggers, pattern selection (Supervisor/Orchestrator with 3 workers, respecting the 3-5 worker cap gotcha), the forward_message telephone-game mitigation copied and applied from the skill's own code example, the instruction-passing-by-default / file-system-memory-on-escalation isolation choice, an error-propagation validation checkpoint between the Technical and Billing agents, a 3-hop TTL limit, a note on why consensus/voting is out of scope here, and a token-budget caveat referencing the skill's 15x guidance. Ends with a summary decision table mapping each decision to the specific skill section that justified it. Verified by re-reading design.md after writing it and confirming it renders as a complete, internally consistent architecture document with no missing sections. This is exactly the kind of deliverable the skill exists to produce (an architecture design/decision document, not a runnable system), so no code execution or binary output was ever needed -- the task was fully achievable with text file read/write alone.
